$comment: The harness CLI, machine-readable. tests/contract.test.ts fails when this list and src/cli.ts disagree, when a workflow uses a command or flag not marked stable, or when docs/contract.md omits a stable one. stable: true is covered by the compatibility promise in docs/contract.md; stable: false may change in a minor release.

commands.name: run
commands.summary: Start both stacks, capture, compare, claim, gate, report.

commands.name: compare
commands.summary: Re-run normalise/compare/claim/gate on captures already on disk.

commands.name: images
commands.summary: Per image: use it if local, else pull it and verify its cosign signature by digest, else build it from the monorepo ref.

commands.name: mutants
commands.summary: Build every mutant from the base reader image and prove the harness catches each.

commands.name: version
commands.summary: Harness version, git sha, contract version.

commands.name: journeys
commands.summary: List the journeys.

commands.name: stack
commands.summary: Start or stop both compose stacks.

commands.name: kind
commands.summary: The kind substrate.

commands.name: doctor
commands.summary: What this machine lacks to run the harness, and how to install it. Exit 0 ready, 1 a needed tool is missing, 2 usage.

commands.name: noise
commands.summary: The local noise store: the noise branch as a directory. record appends a night and keeps the ratchet; status says whether the latest status licenses a FAIL; history (not stable) prints the ratchet and the streak.

commands.name: guard
commands.summary: The CI guards (masks land in their own PR; an engine change needs a version bump; since 1.11.0, not stable: scoreboard/*.jsonl only gains lines) against a local ref. all runs every guard.

commands.name: override
commands.summary: The local, append-only record of overridden FAILs (the harness-override issues, locally).

commands.name: vuln-db
commands.summary: The pinned vulnerability database (grype's): update fetches it into HARNESS_VULN_DB_DIR, else HARNESS_HOME/vuln-db (the only place a database is ever updated: before a run, never during one); status says which database a scan would read, its build time, age and checksum.

commands.name: prune
commands.summary: Remove run directories under out/ older than --older-than-days and outside the newest --keep-last of their mode, and an image cache older than --image-cache-days. A dry run unless --yes; never touches HARNESS_HOME state, the run in progress or the newest release run that did not FAIL.

commands.name: reports
commands.summary: Keep a run's report.json, report.md and report.html under <store>/reports/<ranAt>-<mode>/ and list it in <store>/reports/index.json, newest first, so it outlives the artifact; --keep-last drops older runs, never one younger than --keep-days (since 1.16.0). Since 1.13.1 a release run with its confidence.json beside it (and changes.json) is kept with them, report.md and report.html led by the Gate, the RCS and its band, the glance and the change risk per PR, and its entry carries confidence and changes. Since 1.16.0 --migration and --upgrade keep the run's rehearsals beside it, and the kept confidence.json links them there.

commands.name: preview
commands.summary: Main to RC: decide what main-preview.yml judges (production from the monorepo's reader overlay, the candidate from main's newest commit with signed images), skipping a pair this harness version already judged unless --force.

commands.name: scorecard
commands.summary: A 0-100 score with every deduction, the A/A normalness, EARS Rule -> diffs -> PRs, and at most five pages to test by hand, from one run's report.json. Informational: never changes a verdict or an exit code.

commands.name: local
commands.summary: One command per maintainer task, planned from the same harness commands the workflows run; --dry-run prints the plan. smoke (since 1.4.0) is the two-stacks smoke of ci.yml. compare (since 1.4.0) is the gate's release step with main against the last release (the highest X.Y.Z present for all four apps on quay.io), 3 runs, no claims by default; an exploration, so it exits 0 whenever a report was produced, 2 when it could not judge, 1 for a harness fault, and --strict makes the exit follow the verdict like gate.

commands.name: release
commands.summary: A pushed candidate to a report with nothing asked: resolve (the baseline from --baseline, release/deployed.json in the monorepo checkout or HARNESS_PRODUCTION_TAG; images ensure), noise (the local store's A/A when clean and at most 7 days old, else an A/A of the baseline), changes (harness changes in the monorepo checkout, since 1.10.0: changes.json, which the score reads as change risk; skipped without a checkout), release (3 runs, k6 20x30s, claims, rules), rehearse (migration, upgrade), score (confidence.json, since 1.9.0), report, led by the Gate, then the RCS and its band. Writes out/<timestamp>-release-command/ (status.json as it goes, report.md, report.html, gate.md, gate.json, confidence.json, changes.json) whatever happened; Ctrl-C takes the stacks down first. --fast: one run, no load, no rehearsals, not for a go decision. Exit 0 pass or warn, 1 FAIL, 2 not judged or usage.

commands.name: changes
commands.summary: The change signals between two tags of the monorepo (git log A..B in the checkout, --monorepo or HARNESS_MONOREPO_DIR; 16.2.2 finds v16.2.2), one risk line per PR: churn per app against its median over the last --history releases, hotspots, files with 3+ authors, orphan changes (CHANGELOG.md or --changelog, pnpm release:changelog --json), test lines per production line, approving reviews (GitHub, GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN), major dependency bumps. Change risk is 100 minus the sum of the PRs' deductions; a signal it cannot read is not measured. --out writes changes.json. Advisory: exit 0 whatever it found, 2 for what it cannot read.

commands.name: confidence
commands.summary: The Release Confidence Score of a release run (its directory, its report.json, or a harness release directory): writes confidence.json beside it and prints the board. The Gate first; then the RCS (0-100, only when the Gate is PASS or WARN) and its band (Green >= 90, Amber 75-89, Red < 75); then eight weighted dimensions, each with every point lost and its evidence. A dimension without its input is not measured and left out of the mean; a breached floor caps the RCS at 74. Advisory: never changes a verdict or an exit code. Since 1.12.0 it also ranks the reviewer's glance into confidence.json (--scoreboard, default HARNESS_HOME/scoreboard/releases.jsonl, is the history novelty reads). Since 1.18.0 --test-signal also reads the monorepo's quality record (quality/<sha>.json) as it is, one with no packages being not measured, and --mutants <mutants.jsonl> joins the newest weekly mutants self-test as harnessMutants when the record has packages. Exit 0 when written, 2 for an input it cannot read.

commands.name: scoreboard
commands.summary: The release scoreboard, one line per release run in releases.jsonl (--file; default HARNESS_HOME/scoreboard/releases.jsonl), append-only: a re-run appends the same tag with the next run number. append builds the line from a scored run (--run: a harness release directory or a confidence.json; a --fast run is refused); trends prints the six views and the run rules (three consecutive declines, or two of three releases below 75, in a dimension or the RCS, opens a kaizen item) beside the harness's own health, and --site writes scoreboard.html and scoreboard.json; mutants records a self-test's mutants.json in mutants.jsonl. Advisory: exit 0 when done, 2 for what it cannot read.

commands.name: glance
commands.summary: The reviewer's glance (SOP step 8, gemba): at most seven places to look, ranked by novelty x exposure in confidence.json by the score, each linked to the hunk, the claim and the PR. mark records verified, disputed (becomes a new claim or a hold) or escalated (becomes a 5 Whys) for one item in glance-marks.jsonl beside confidence.json and re-renders the glance in confidence.json, report.md, gate.md and report.html; status prints the glance with its marks and whether an Amber release's glance is recorded verified. Marks never change the Gate or an exit code. mark: exit 0 when recorded, 2 for what it cannot use; status: exit 0 always once --run is given (informational).

commands.name: why
commands.summary: The 5 Whys (kaizen). With --run <run dir | harness release dir> --finding <id> [--out kaizen/] [--tag T] [--scoreboard f]: writes <out>/<date>-<tag>-<finding>.md with Why 1 answered from the run's own trace (the finding, artefact, journeys, hunk link, nearest claim and why it did not cover, the PR with its files and churn, a first contribution as a fact, the glance rank and mark), Whys 2-5 blank and the countermeasure constrained to seven kinds (mutant, journey, mask review, EARS spec, claim guidance, SOP change, glance rule); --finding is gate, band, rollback, <rule>:<series>, countermeasures-rising, a glance item (<kind>:<key> or glance:<n>) or a hunk id; a file already there is left alone. check <file|dir...>: exit 1 when a filled 5 Whys is not ready (an answer missing up to where the chain ends, an answer that is only human error, carelessness or a person's name, a chain not ending in a process or a tool, not exactly one of the seven kinds, a mutant without its path under mutants/, no owner or due date); a docs lint, never a release gate. register [--dir kaizen] [--write]: regenerates the table of kaizen/README.md from the files, with the open and overdue counts; without --write, exit 1 when README.md is out of date. harness release opens one by itself for a Gate FAIL, a Red band, a run rule firing and open countermeasures only rising; harness glance mark for an escalated mark. Exit 2 for what it cannot read.

commands.name: a3
commands.summary: The A3 Aggregator: one Lean A3 from every kept run under --site (each stream's reports/index.json and the reports beside it), the kaizen register (--kaizen, default kaizen/), the noise history (--noise-history), the scoreboard (--scoreboard) and, with --fetch-github (GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN) or a snapshot (--github), the value stream workflows' history on GitHub. Writes a3.html and a3.json (and github.json when it asked GitHub) into --site: the Gate and the RCS as confidence.json has them, a value stream map, Paretos of the unclaimed differences, the line stops, the confidence lost and the change risk, root cause questions linked to the 5 Whys that answer them, and the countermeasures, plan and follow-up. Since 1.18.0 the quality strip under the Gate: Speed, Metrics and Tests, each within reason, look or not measured, from the subject run's report.json, the monorepo's quality record kept beside it and the weekly mutants (--mutants, default mutants.jsonl beside --scoreboard). What it cannot read is said to be not measured. Advisory: never an input to the Gate, a verdict or an exit code. Exit 0 when written, 2 for what it cannot read.

commands.name: readiness
commands.summary: The overnight readiness page: one row per calendar night (UTC) for the last ten nights, newest on top, from the Main to RC forecasts under --site (main-preview/reports/index.json and the kept reports beside it): the commit judged (with its full sha and image digests), the Gate, the unclaimed count, the delta since the previous forecast beside the same production, and links to the kept report and its rehearsals. A night that kept nothing is read from the workflow history (the site's github.json, as harness a3 --fetch-github writes it, or --github): unchanged since a commit, shown in grey with the verdict it repeats; not judged; did not run; or not known without the history. The band is left off. Since 1.18.0 each forecast carries the quality strip as marks (Speed, Metrics, Tests; --mutants <mutants.jsonl> for the Tests mark's weekly self-test), and the latest the whole strip. Since 1.19.0 the page leads with the release-size control chart: each past release of the monorepo in merged PRs, its XmR limits (centre = mean, UCL = mean + 2.66 x mean moving range, LCL = max(0, mean - 2.66 x mean moving range); provisional under 10 releases, when the WIP limit is the centre line), the PRs on main not yet released in a zone named in words (below the centre line, a good time to release, release now) and the count night by night, as `control` in readiness.json; --fetch-releases asks GitHub (GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN) for the release sizes and writes releases.json into --site, --releases <f> reads one. Since 1.25.0 the soak toward 2.0, as `soak` in readiness.json: clean nights in a row since 2026-10-02 (every nightly A/A that night clean and verified, from --noise-history <noise-history.json>, default noise/noise-history.json in --site, and that night's forecast's a-to-a2 clean; a night Main to RC skipped pauses the count; anything else breaks it) against the target of 10, and per policy check its quiet nights and its planted mutant (caught, escaped, not run yet). Writes readiness.html and readiness.json into --site. Advisory: never an input to the Gate, a verdict, an engine level or an exit code. Exit 0 when written, 2 for what it cannot read.

imageSpecs.$comment: What --a, --b and --base accept outside migration mode (src/image-ref.ts). Since 1.1.0: @sha256 digests. Since 1.3.0: the time app.
forms: <repo>:<tag>[@sha256:<64 hex>] - that app; the others take the prefix and the tag
reader=<ref>,catalogue=<ref>,live=<ref>[,time=<ref>] - each <ref> is <repo>[:<tag>][@sha256:<64 hex>]; time is optional since 1.3.0 and takes the reader's tag when left out
refused: <repo>@sha256:... on its own - no tag for the other apps to take

environment.$comment: Environment variables that are part of the contract. Since 1.1.0, except HARNESS_IMAGE_PREFIX (whose {app} template form is since 1.1.0), the SBOM, vulnerability and static-artefact variables (since 1.2.0) and HARNESS_HOME, HARNESS_PROJECT, HARNESS_COMPOSE_PROJECT and HARNESS_KIND_CLUSTER (since 1.3.0), and HARNESS_VULN_DB_MAX_AGE_DAYS, HARNESS_ROLLBACK_ISSUE and HARNESS_REQUIRE_ARTEFACTS (since 1.4.0).

HARNESS_IMAGE_PREFIX.meaning: prefix (<prefix>/<app>:<tag>) or template containing {app}, for bare tags; --image-prefix overrides

HARNESS_COSIGN_IDENTITY.meaning: regular expression the signing certificate's identity must match; empty means the default

HARNESS_COSIGN_ISSUER.meaning: OIDC issuer of the signing certificate; empty means the default

HARNESS_PROJECT.meaning: since 1.3.0. The name of this checkout's docker compose project and kind cluster, when HARNESS_COMPOSE_PROJECT / HARNESS_KIND_CLUSTER do not say. Unset, the name is tutors-harness-<the first 8 hex of sha256 of the checkout's real path, lowercased on Windows>, so two checkouts or worktrees never share a stack

HARNESS_COMPOSE_PROJECT.meaning: since 1.3.0 (an override that existed before it). The docker compose project this checkout's stack runs under; wins over HARNESS_PROJECT. Empty means the derived name. It is never the machine owner's own project, which the harness never touches

HARNESS_KIND_CLUSTER.meaning: since 1.3.0 (an override that existed before it). The kind cluster name; wins over HARNESS_PROJECT. Empty means the derived name. The name tutors-harness, which every checkout used before 1.3.0, is refused: a cluster of that name is not adopted or deleted by any harness command

HARNESS_HOME.meaning: since 1.3.0. Where the harness keeps what outlives a run on this machine: noise/ (the default source of --noise in release and post-deploy mode, when --noise is omitted), releases/ (the release records), overrides.jsonl, image-cache/

HARNESS_CLAIM_MAX_HUNKS.meaning: since 1.2.0: a claim covering more failing hunks than this is flagged in claimHygiene; a positive integer, else the default; --claim-max-hunks overrides

HARNESS_SBOM_SOURCE.meaning: since 1.2.0. Where the SBOM of each image comes from: auto or attestation (the SPDX attestation cosign attached to a pulled image), or generate (a local generator run over the image on both sides)

HARNESS_SBOM_CMD.default: syft docker:{image} -o spdx-json (on a Windows host: the same syft run in its anchore/syft container over the Docker socket)
HARNESS_SBOM_CMD.meaning: since 1.2.0. The SBOM generator for HARNESS_SBOM_SOURCE=generate; {image} is the image reference; prints SPDX JSON on stdout. Split on whitespace and quotes, run without a shell

HARNESS_VULN_CMD.meaning: since 1.2.0. The vulnerability scanner; {sbom} is the path of the image's SPDX SBOM; prints grype or trivy JSON on stdout

HARNESS_VULN_DB_DIR.meaning: since 1.2.0. A pre-fetched scanner database directory (GRYPE_DB_CACHE_DIR / TRIVY_CACHE_DIR). Scanner database updates are always switched off, so this is what pins the scan. Since 1.4.0, unset means HARNESS_HOME/vuln-db when `harness vuln-db update` has made it, else the scanner's own cache

HARNESS_THIRD_PARTY_CACHE_DIR.meaning: since 1.5.0. Where the recorded responses of the third-party hosts the apps load in the browser (Google Fonts, Iconify, cdn.jsdelivr.net) are kept: fetched once, then every request on both sides and in later runs is answered from the record. Delete the directory to record afresh

HARNESS_VULN_DB_MAX_AGE_DAYS.meaning: since 1.4.0. How old (days since built) the vulnerability database may be: `harness doctor` warns beyond it, and it is passed to grype as its own limit (GRYPE_DB_MAX_ALLOWED_BUILT_AGE), so a scan and the doctor agree. 5 is grype's own default

HARNESS_ROLLBACK_ISSUE.meaning: since 1.4.0. Post-deploy wording only: 1 | true | yes says a CI step opens a rollback issue on a FAIL (the reason says 'open a rollback issue'); 0 | false | no says none does (the reason says 'decide whether to roll back'). Unset: GitHub Actions (GITHUB_ACTIONS=true) has the step, anything else does not

HARNESS_REQUIRE_ARTEFACTS.meaning: since 1.4.0. Comma separated artefacts (image-manifest, sbom, vulns, runtime, startup, bus), or static, or all, whose 'not collected' gap is a failing hunk instead of an informational one. Adds to what is already required (runtime, startup); an unknown name is exit 2

HARNESS_MONOREPO_DIR.meaning: since 1.8.0. The monorepo checkout harness release reads release/deployed.json (the baseline, when --baseline is prod or omitted) and release/claims.yaml (when --claims is omitted) from; --monorepo overrides

HARNESS_REQUIRE_STATIC.meaning: 1 | true | yes (since 1.2.0): an alias for HARNESS_REQUIRE_ARTEFACTS=static; the two add up

exitCodes.0: verdict pass or warn, or a fail overridden with --override-reason; or the command succeeded
exitCodes.1: verdict fail that was not overridden; or images ensure could not obtain an image, or mutants or kind rollout did not succeed; or doctor found a tool a run needs missing, noise record found the ratchet broken, noise status --require found a status that does not license a FAIL, or guard found a violation
exitCodes.2: usage error, the harness itself failed (an uncaught error), or an image may not be judged; no verdict was reached
